clue.text: Windy indigestion and endless farts causing confusion

indicators.note: windy suggests something blown about and churned up, so the letters are tossed into a new order
a word with no ends has lost the letters at both its front and its back

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before both ends are trimmed

explanation.surface: A crude complaint that flatulence and an upset stomach leave you all at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Trimming both ends of FARTS leaves ART, which is shuffled together with INDIGESTION to give DISORIENTATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disorientating leaves a person bewildered, so the participle means bringing about bewilderment.

clue.text: Senior coppers and judge secure noble financial arrangement

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the outer letters grip the noble in their middle

blocks.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors, senior police officers
to rate is to judge or assess
a count is a nobleman

explanation.surface: Top police officers and a judge are said to have locked up an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: DIS and RATE together go around COUNT. DI stands for Detective Inspector in British police ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A discount rate is the interest rate a central bank charges, a fixed term in banking and lending.

clue.text: Small bird is to leave pronto

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a coot is a black water bird

explanation.surface: A little bird is about to take off in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoot is informally to go away quickly, a synonym for departing in haste.

clue.text: Terrific new energy charges electrical device

indicators.note: something made new has been remade, so the word is rebuilt in a fresh order
to charge something is to load or fill it, so the rearranged word takes a letter inside

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Fresh power fills up a marvellous gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like the electrical sense, fitting the surface, but it means loads: the E goes inside the rearranged TERRIFIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectifier is a component that converts alternating current into direct current.

clue.text: Cockney intellectual mentioned a feature on his boat?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial h, so the word is said with its first sound missing
something mentioned is spoken, so we go by how the word is pronounced

blocks.note: a highbrow is an intellectual, said without its h

explanation.surface: A clever Londoner talks about some detail of his vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boat' is Cockney rhyming slang: boat race means face. So a feature on his boat is a facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebrow is a feature of the face, and in rhyming slang a face is a boat.

clue.text: Returned books about dress on a Russian empress

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the books are read from right to left
about means around, so the books go around the dress

blocks.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books
a sari is a draped dress worn in South Asia
taken as written

explanation.surface: Library books brought back with something about a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the books are turned round: TN wraps SARI, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar, an empress of Russia.

clue.text: Available gents, perhaps one dropping out

indicators.note: something dropping out leaves, so that letter is taken away from the word

blocks.note: the gents is a men's toilet; 'perhaps' marks it as one example
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A free loo, one person leaving it.
explanation.walkthrough: TOILET without its I gives TO LET. 'The gents' is the British term for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A property marked 'to let' is up for rent, so it is open to be taken.

clue.text: Sky Sport in Bremen broadcast over grand German city

indicators.note: to sky is to send upwards, and in a down clue going upwards reads the word backwards
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
in places one piece inside the other
in a down clue, over means above, so the first part sits on top of the next

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
taken as written, then rearranged
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A sports channel shown in one German city covers a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky Sport' looks like the TV channel, but 'Sky' means send upwards, which in a down clue reverses the sport. In a down clue 'over' puts one part above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuremberg (Nürnberg) is a large city in Bavaria, in southern Germany.

clue.text: Head of innovation in store nearly resigned

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, which here is the piece placed inside
in places one piece within the other
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: the first letter of innovation
stock is a store or supply of goods

explanation.surface: A shop's new ideas chief has almost quit.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCK loses its final K to give STOC, and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic person accepts hardship without complaint, as someone resigned to their fate does.

clue.text: We make possible clothing for Afghan rebels somehow

definitions.note: a clause standing for a plural noun: those who make things possible

indicators.note: clothing is what wraps the outside, so only the outermost letters are kept
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters can be put in any order

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Afghan
taken as written

explanation.surface: Suppliers boast that they somehow kit out insurgents in Afghanistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Enablers are people who allow something to happen, so they are the ones making it possible.

clue.text: Removal of hard skin from undercoat and its base

indicators.note: base means debased or corrupt, so the letters are spoilt out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter's job of stripping a hardened coat back to the primer beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' reads as a base coat of paint, fitting the undercoat; it is the anagram signal. The answer also rearranges 1 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrustation is the taking off of a crust, a hardened outer layer.

clue.text: It's far from mean to expose perjurer that's escaped from trap

indicators.note: trap is slang for mouth, and what escapes the mouth is speech, so go by the sound

blocks.note: to out someone is to expose them
a perjurer is a liar, said aloud

explanation.surface: Exposing a lying witness who has slipped a snare is anything but cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' is the statistical average, not unkind. 'Trap' is slang for mouth, so words escaping it are spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlier is a data point lying well away from the average of a set.

clue.text: Vessel linings close after latest temperature's dropped

indicators.note: a dropped letter falls out, so it is taken away from the word

blocks.note: intimate means close, as in a friendship
T for temperature; latest says it is the later of the two Ts that goes

explanation.surface: A forecast of the hull's lining, close once the latest reading fell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' sounds nautical, but it is a blood vessel. Dropping the second T from INTIMATE gives INTIMAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimae is the Latin plural of intima, the innermost layer of an artery or vein.

clue.text: China ominously detains girl

indicators.note: to detain is to hold in custody, so the words hold the answer within them

blocks.note: found running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A sinister report that Beijing is holding a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female given name, and crosswords freely use girl to stand for any woman's name.

clue.text: Passages in Poe so bad, old lady is skipping the second half

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the letters are put in the wrong order
skipping means leaving out, and the second half of a two-letter word is its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a hag is an ugly old woman
taken as written, before half is dropped

explanation.surface: A reader complains that Edgar Allan Poe writes so poorly that an elderly reader skips ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passages' looks like passages of text, fitting Poe, but they are body passages.
explanation.definitionFit: The oesophagi (gullets) are the tubes carrying food from throat to stomach, anatomical passages.

clue.text: Teacher who almost messed up old greeting

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is left off
something messed up is in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A teacher who nearly made a mess of saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: WHO without its O joins TEACHER for the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: 'What cheer' is an archaic salutation, the ancestor of the Cockney 'wotcha', so it is a dated hello.

clue.text: Shrimps etc. in saucer cat licked

indicators.note: licked means beaten or thrashed, so the letters are knocked about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seafood left in a dish that the cat has licked clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Licked' looks like the cat eating; it means beaten, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Crustacea is the class of animals including shrimps, crabs and lobsters, so the shrimps are examples.

clue.text: Republican stratagem backing female, one that's come out of hiding

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the stratagem is read from right to left

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
a ruse is a stratagem or trick
F is the abbreviation for female
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A political trick to support a woman candidate who has broken cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like supporting the female; it means the stratagem runs backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To resurface is to reappear after being out of sight, as a person emerging from hiding does.

clue.text: Side by side, having run into a depraved individual

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the run is placed within the other piece

blocks.note: a beast is a brutal or depraved person
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Two people walk together after bumping into a brute.
explanation.definitionFit: Abreast means level with each other and facing the same way, as in walking two abreast.

clue.text: US marshal to carry impediment to hearing

blocks.note: Wyatt Earp was a famous lawman of the American West
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: A Wild West lawman hauling along a court obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' tempts a reading as a court hearing, fitting the marshal; it is the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: An earplug is put in the ear to block sound, so it stops a person hearing.

clue.text: Without pressure, clears out drives

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to purge is to clear out or empty

explanation.surface: Taking it easy, someone decluttering their driveways.
explanation.definitionFit: Urges are strong impulses that push a person on, the same sense as inner drives.

clue.text: TV programme, the fastest on the box?

blocks.note: first meaning: the long-running BBC motoring show
second meaning: the highest ratio in a gearbox, the one for maximum speed

explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' reads as television, matching the show; here it is the gearbox, and the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Gear is a BBC car programme, and top gear is the highest gear, used for the greatest speed.

clue.text: Pennine unit intermittently displays tedium

indicators.note: intermittently means on and off, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A unit stationed in the Pennine hills is bored stiff now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pennines are a range of hills in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loan word for listless boredom, a synonym of tedium.

clue.text: Infestation picked up beneath circular building

indicators.note: picked up as in heard on a radio, so we go by the sound of the word

blocks.note: dry rot and wet rot are fungal infestations of timber
beneath means under, said with a non-rhotic British accent

explanation.surface: Vermin were found lurking under a round structure.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound trick relies on a British accent where the final R of under is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, typically one topped by a dome.

clue.text: Northern drivers beginning to frequent independent canteen

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motorists' organisation
the first letter of frequent
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: Motorists from the north often call in at a café run by an independent.
explanation.walkthrough: The NAAFI is the organisation running shops and canteens for the British armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The NAAFI is known to British service personnel as their base canteen, so the name stands for one.

clue.text: Weather data filter left by day attached to zip lines

indicators.note: left by means abandoned by, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: to drain is to filter liquid off
D is the abbreviation for day
FA as in 'sweet FA', meaning nothing at all
ll. is the abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: Meteorological readings sifted daily and linked to zip-wire courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zip lines' looks like a single thing, but zip and lines are separate pieces. 'Sweet FA' is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainfall is the measured amount of rain over a period, a standard statistic recorded by meteorologists.

clue.text: Separated from leader, ran away from Croatian animal

indicators.note: going away from somewhere means leaving it, so these letters are taken out
warns that the letters to be removed are not side by side, and one of them sits right next to the opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written: the letters to remove
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beast fled from a Croatian, cut off from its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters R, A, N are not together: the R is separated from AN, and sits just after the leading C.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a racoon-like mammal of the Americas with a long snout and ringed tail.

clue.text: Slag off essentially fine first goal, overturned in loss of cohesion

indicators.note: the essence is the core, so only the middle of the word is kept
something overturned is upside down, so these pieces are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to dis someone is to insult or slag them off
the core of fine
No. 1 means first
a target is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Badmouthing a decent opening score as the team falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slag off' is British slang for criticise. 'First' gives NO I, written number one, before reversing with TARGET.
explanation.definitionFit: Disintegration is the breaking apart of something into fragments, a loss of what holds it together.
